items.title: Gujarat High Court restores ban on non-veg eateries near Somnath Temple hours after single-judge lifts ban
items.summary: A Gujarat High Court division bench on Friday restored a ban on the preparation, sale and storage of non-vegetarian food around Somnath Temple. [State of Gujarat & Ors. v Taj Restaurant Owner Aakib Aminbhai Khan & Ors.] . A division bench of Acting Chief Justice (ACJ) Manash Ranjan Pathak and Justice Nirzar S Desai stayed an order passed by a single-judge hours after the latter passed the judgment lifting the ban. This was after the State moved in appeal against the single-judge's order immediately after it was pronounced. The single-judge's verdict had not yet been published on the Court website when the State's appeal came up for hearing. The division bench took up the State's appeal at around 5.30 pm, barely two-and-a-half hours after single-judge Justice Nisha M Thakore pronounced her verdict at around 3 pm. The District Magistrate had issued a preliminary notification on July 10, inviting objections to a proposed prohibition on the preparation, sale and storage of meat, fish and non-vegetarian dishes at shops, restaurants, hotels and roadside stalls in specified areas.
